scope: Documentation-only readiness audit; source-backed risks and opportunities, not a new vulnerability certification or performance qualification.

severity_policy.Critical: Established catastrophic authority/correctness failure requiring stop; none found in scoped audit.
severity_policy.High: Blocks stated large-workload, sustained-operation or reproducible release goals.
severity_policy.Medium: Material optimization, lifecycle or release-maintenance gap; no established authority bypass.
severity_policy.Low: Conditional future improvement or visibility gap.

gaps.title: No reproducible end-to-end performance baseline
gaps.current_behavior: Scope 5 qualifies correctness and authority, not performance distributions or incremental crossover.
gaps.risk: Optimizations and large-workload claims cannot be evaluated objectively.
gaps.recommended_change: Establish seeded fixtures, stage timings, cold/warm paired runs and machine-readable manifests before optimization.
gaps.security_impact: Timing must remain descriptive and cannot authorize actions.
gaps.performance_impact: Makes CPU/transfer/queue/context/kernel costs separately measurable.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce B1-B7 with fixture/environment/source digests and per-run samples.
Publish paired crossover confidence intervals; no kernel-only speed claim.

gaps.title: Qualified motif scale is far below requested large-graph targets
gaps.current_behavior: 256-edge/100000-incidence limits coexist with I*(E-1)*(E-2)/2<=5000000; nonempty rows imply E<=216. STATIC launches E^3 slots; incremental host enumerates all triples.
gaps.risk: 10k/100k edges and 1M incidences cannot be claimed as qualified motif inputs; increasing limits would expose combinatorial work.
gaps.recommended_change: Keep current ceilings. Prototype scalable candidate/work algorithms only in a separately qualified native phase.
gaps.security_impact: Preserve independent safe arithmetic, allocation bounds, exact taxonomy and delta semantics.
gaps.performance_impact: Main barrier to large motif workloads; speedups inside current envelope alone do not establish scale.
acceptance_criteria: Current boundaries still reject at browser, Runtime and native layers.
Any new envelope has independent work/memory bounds, 30-bin parity and live device qualification.

gaps.title: Large DynamicHypergraph staging depends on a bounded motif projection
gaps.current_behavior: Pending validation computes full graph preview then always canonicalizes OLD/proposed with 256-edge/100000-incidence limits, even before deciding motifImpact NONE.
gaps.risk: Generic representation capacity is not large DynamicHypergraph Stage/Apply capacity; rejection occurs after expensive preview.
gaps.recommended_change: First reject oversized pending work cheaply and document the product envelope. Separately design explicit unavailable-analysis state if larger editing is needed; no implicit projection.
gaps.security_impact: GraphMutationPlan stays sole Apply authority. New unavailable transport state needs explicit schema/currentness review.
gaps.performance_impact: Avoids full preview before known resource rejection; larger editing remains a separately gated contract change.
acceptance_criteria: Oversized Stage rejects before full proposed-state clone/hash work.
No-op, metadata-only, replay and Apply-without-analysis regressions pass.
Larger editing is not advertised unless explicit state semantics are qualified.

gaps.title: Undo history retains up to fifty full graph snapshots
gaps.current_behavior: 25 rolling history events each independently JSON-clone before and after graphs.
gaps.risk: Bounded event count still multiplies large-graph heap and per-commit GC cost.
gaps.recommended_change: Add byte-aware retention and immutable sharing/checkpoints where justified; retain exact undo identity/type behavior.
gaps.security_impact: Undo remains a fresh committed transition, never a revival of prior executable authority.
gaps.performance_impact: Reduces O(25*I) retained snapshots and repeated stringify/parse.
acceptance_criteria: History obeys count and byte budgets after 1000/10000 commits.
Undo content/type parity and replacement/currentness tests pass.

gaps.title: Repeated whole-graph cloning, canonicalization and hashing
gaps.current_behavior: Mutation engine clones all rows; preview counts both graphs; pending digest/freezing copy proposed state; analysis Stage and submit independently prepare OLD/NEW; Apply rederives.
gaps.risk: Main-thread work and transient duplicate data increase despite small edits.
gaps.recommended_change: Measure then share immutable revision-bound products, reuse exact canonical bytes and skip demonstrably unnecessary comparison work while preserving collision-safe checks.
gaps.security_impact: Never replace exact content comparison with the short FNV marker; no cache may bypass live base/revision/session checks.
gaps.performance_impact: Reduces repeated O(I+E log E+sum k log k) work and allocation.
acceptance_criteria: Stage/Apply p95 and peak heap measured against unchanged fixtures.
Same-marker/different-content collision and late async tests pass.
Cache ownership and invalidation are explicit and bounded.

gaps.title: Preview edge budgets do not bound vertices or membership processing
gaps.current_behavior: Viz slices edges, then builds topology from all selected memberships; overlay copies all rows before sampling. Vertex list renders every selected vertex and hyperedge list uses indexOf inside map.
gaps.risk: One huge edge can allocate and render enormous vertex sets despite the 3000-relation overlay budget; high-edge display can create quadratic lookup work.
gaps.recommended_change: Bound visual vertices/incidences before materialization; virtualize lists; hoist selection membership work; keep sampled visualization separate from exact analytical data.
gaps.security_impact: Sampling never changes graph, motifs or Apply; explicit incomplete presentation required.
gaps.performance_impact: Highest browser rendering risk for skewed inputs.
acceptance_criteria: Huge-single-edge preview obeys explicit vertex/incidence/DOM budgets.
Search/selection/accessibility and exact analytical export remain correct.
Manual browser responsive interaction gate passes.

gaps.title: Artifact bytes are serialized twice and base64 expanded
gaps.current_behavior: Workflow stringifies/hashes artifacts but uploads original objects; client stringifies again, creates UTF-8 bytes, a binary string, base64 and a JSON envelope.
gaps.risk: Transient strings and ~4/3 transfer amplification; nominal 6MiB artifact exceeds 8MiB request after envelope overhead.
gaps.recommended_change: Reuse exact hashed bytes first; calculate encoded envelope limit. Consider versioned raw-byte upload only after measured justification.
gaps.security_impact: Digest covers exact bytes; streamed protocol must retain admission and hash-before-publication.
gaps.performance_impact: Reduces duplicate serialization and upload cost without changing native semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Measured HTTP bytes match deterministic base64/envelope arithmetic.
Near-limit artifacts reject before large duplicate construction.
Protocol compatibility and exact digest substitutions are tested.

gaps.title: Safe artifact reuse is absent at the browser boundary
gaps.current_behavior: Exact artifacts deduplicate retained Runtime storage, but workflow rehashes/reuploads the same OLD graph and exact revision; client exposes no artifact metadata lookup.
gaps.risk: Repeated analysis wastes CPU, transfer and disk verification.
gaps.recommended_change: Use bounded tab-local exact-byte cache and Runtime-session-scoped presence handles; verify digest/media/length and upload on cache miss.
gaps.security_impact: Rebind every analysis to fresh request/confirmation/current graph/revision/session; cached data grants no authority.
gaps.performance_impact: Saves repeated serialization/upload on unchanged committed graph or exact pending revision.
acceptance_criteria: Repeat analysis avoids graph upload when exact artifact is verified present.
Restart, eviction, media mismatch, cross-tab and stale revision cannot reuse authority.
No transparent result-authority replay.

gaps.title: Runtime job quota is a lifetime session limit
gaps.current_behavior: jobs Map retains all terminal and active records; maxJobs=256 is checked before dedup and no terminal eviction exists.
gaps.risk: Analyzed 1000/10000-update sessions cannot complete without Runtime restart; terminal cancellation also consumes quota.
gaps.recommended_change: Separate active/backlog admission from bounded terminal diagnostics; define expiry/eviction responses and retain artifacts pinned by active/current jobs.
gaps.security_impact: Unknown/expired job IDs fail closed; eviction cannot resurrect results or approvals.
gaps.performance_impact: Restores sustained throughput while bounding retained memory.
acceptance_criteria: At least 1000 sequential jobs complete in one session under retention budget.
Active/current jobs are not evicted and expired result requests reject.
Cancelled/failed jobs release active capacity.

gaps.title: Artifact retention has quotas but no reclamation policy
gaps.current_behavior: 512 artifacts/64MiB default retained quotas have no eviction. Auto temp roots dispose on graceful close; override roots persist and metadata is not reconstructed.
gaps.risk: Store may fill before job limit; persistent roots accumulate files outside current metadata accounting across restarts.
gaps.recommended_change: Introduce pin-aware byte/count LRU or TTL, accurate persisted-root accounting, explicit cleanup and privacy policy.
gaps.security_impact: No unvalidated cross-session presence; pin through result acceptance; hash every reused artifact as required.
gaps.performance_impact: Prevents quota exhaustion and orphan disk growth; enables reliable reuse.
acceptance_criteria: Long runs keep stored bytes/items within declared budgets.
Pinned artifacts survive; corrupted/unregistered files never become authorized.
Restart and graceful/abrupt cleanup policies are tested.

gaps.title: Per-item bounds leave aggregate admission work unbounded
gaps.current_behavior: HTTP buffers each body; artifact put copies before queued quota checks; qualified backend verification precedes job quota admission. No explicit total in-flight byte/request budget found.
gaps.risk: Authenticated flooding may amplify concurrent heap, queued copies and qualification work; harmful impact has not been runtime demonstrated.
gaps.recommended_change: Reserve aggregate bytes/work before decoding/copy/verification; bound concurrent admission and release reservations on every abort/error.
gaps.security_impact: Keep loopback/auth/origin boundary and individual limits; do not label this unauthenticated remote access.
gaps.performance_impact: Protects host responsiveness and predictable throughput under burst load.
acceptance_criteria: Authenticated concurrent uploads/submits stay within explicit aggregate limits.
Partial bodies/abort/cancel release reservations.
Unauthenticated requests cannot allocate protected upload buffers.

gaps.title: Queue residence and shared GPU scheduling lack explicit budgets
gaps.current_behavior: Motif jobs serialize on one Promise chain; SSSP bypasses it. Native timeout begins after queue wait and preparation.
gaps.risk: Native timeout is not user-latency SLA; cross-backend or external GPU contention remains possible.
gaps.recommended_change: Bound backlog and queue wait, define end-to-end deadlines and device ownership before adding concurrency.
gaps.security_impact: Expired/cancelled queued jobs never launch or publish results; concurrency cannot defeat fixed device authority.
gaps.performance_impact: Predictable queue latency; parallel motif execution is not recommended initially.
acceptance_criteria: Queued expiry/cancellation prevents native launch.
Device scheduler tests include motif and SSSP coexistence.
Queue and native timing boundaries are separately reported.

gaps.title: Browser Runtime requests lack timeout and transport abort
gaps.current_behavior: Candy client fetch uses no AbortSignal or timeout; logical invalidation safely blocks late acceptance but does not release the outstanding HTTP work.
gaps.risk: Interrupted uploads/discovery/result reads can remain pending and retain captured context.
gaps.recommended_change: Add per-operation bounded deadlines and generation-owned AbortControllers while preserving synchronous local revocation.
gaps.security_impact: Abort is transport cleanup; every async result still needs exact currentness checks.
gaps.performance_impact: Releases hanging requests and captured large data earlier.
acceptance_criteria: Loopback interruption/reconnect/unmount aborts old requests.
Held genuine late result stays rejected.
Retry requires fresh discovery/confirmation as applicable.

gaps.title: Graph-status chat appends bypass the live message bound
gaps.current_behavior: Normal append slices to 500; graph changes and some batch/continuation notices append without slicing. Message render maps the full live array.
gaps.risk: Many commits can exceed live chat cap and grow DOM/serialization cost; persisted 80-message cap does not bound live state.
gaps.recommended_change: Route all appends through one bounded helper and virtualize if 500 rendered messages remain costly.
gaps.security_impact: Pruning historical messages must not create executable action restoration or weaken current approval owner.
gaps.performance_impact: Bounds long-session UI and persistence input cost.
acceptance_criteria: 10000 graph-status transitions keep live messages at or below 500.
Reload remains inert and fresh confirmation ownership unchanged.

gaps.title: Repeated exports leave Blob Object URLs retained
gaps.current_behavior: App dl helper creates an Object URL but never revokes it; parser profile and resolved export downloads call this helper.
gaps.risk: Repeated large exports retain Blob backing storage for the document lifetime.
gaps.recommended_change: Revoke URLs after safe download dispatch and on teardown using a shared bounded helper.
gaps.security_impact: Do not log exported content or mix cleanup with graph authority.
gaps.performance_impact: Eliminates a concrete lifecycle leak for repeated exports.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated downloads leave no retained Object URLs after completion.
Downloaded bytes are unchanged and browser smoke passes.

gaps.title: Thread storage and derived products need byte observability
gaps.current_behavior: Storage is bounded to 80 records of at most 1M serialized characters; two save snapshots; current-graph derived cache clears on transition but has no internal byte budget.
gaps.risk: Count bounds can still consume meaningful quota/heap; no proven unbounded current call-site cache growth.
gaps.recommended_change: Measure persisted bytes/current derived bytes; add budgets only where measured; normalize/project before oversized raw serialization when possible.
gaps.security_impact: Persist only inert descriptions; eviction must not restore graph/update/result authority.
gaps.performance_impact: Improves quota failure handling and visibility; avoids unnecessary cache complexity.
acceptance_criteria: Quota/storage errors remain recoverable and live graph independent.
Save backlog never exceeds one in-flight plus one latest.
Derived products clear on graph transition.

gaps.title: Bounded model prompts still require full local indexes and unbounded response reads
gaps.current_behavior: Mutation planner builds entity index/counts and arrays of all keys before sampling; observations are bounded, but localModelClient response.text reads the entire configured endpoint response.
gaps.risk: Large graphs cost O(I) context preparation; faulty paired private model can cause response memory pressure without gaining action authority.
gaps.recommended_change: Reuse bounded current-graph index/count products; slice iterators before materializing full samples; bound model response bytes independently of timeout.
gaps.security_impact: Never send full graph/plan/result taxonomy; strict selectors and independent approvals stay authoritative.
gaps.performance_impact: Reduces deterministic preparation and caps response memory.
acceptance_criteria: Prompt limits and bounded selectors unchanged across large fixtures.
Oversized model response aborts before full body parsing.
Graph transition invalidates index reuse.

gaps.title: Every analysis repeats qualification, parsing and process/CUDA startup
gaps.current_behavior: Submission verifies backend; launch verifies again; artifacts reread/rehashed/parsed and native process launched per job; native initializes device each process.
gaps.risk: Small kernels may be dominated by host and WSL/process startup, but no measured breakdown establishes dominance yet.
gaps.recommended_change: Measure first; cache integrity-bound prepared immutable host data with bounded ownership. Treat persistent native worker as separate protocol/security project.
gaps.security_impact: Any verification cache must detect binary/source/qualification replacement; fixed argv and cleanup remain enforced.
gaps.performance_impact: Potential repeated-work savings; persistent device state is deferred until launch overhead is proven.
acceptance_criteria: Breakdown reports verification/read/parse/pack/launch/process costs.
Changed binary/evidence disables cached qualification.
No persistent worker introduced without new qualification boundary.

gaps.title: Incremental candidate vectors and fresh device buffers add overhead
gaps.current_behavior: Both OLD/NEW host candidate vectors coexist; OLD and NEW launch sequentially with fresh allocations and synchronous transfers. Kernel timer excludes preparation, allocations and transfers.
gaps.risk: Affected-only GPU work does not guarantee faster end-to-end execution; all-affected updates can duplicate substantial work.
gaps.recommended_change: Profile host enumeration and device lifecycle; test direct affected enumeration, sequential host-vector lifetime and reusable per-process workspace before pools/pinned memory/streams.
gaps.security_impact: Maintain safe products, counts, digest and cleanup; no STATIC fallback or prior-count delta reconstruction.
gaps.performance_impact: Reduces host peak memory and overhead if validated; streams are not yet justified.
acceptance_criteria: Per-class old STATIC plus incremental delta equals new STATIC.
Host/device peak allocations and whole-process time improve under paired tests.
Failure/cancel/driver-reset paths free all workspaces.

gaps.title: Portable packaging policy predates Runtime qualification assets
gaps.current_behavior: Packager scans filesystem files; exclusions omit build/.local although Git ignores them. It excludes .git and artifacts, but production motifQualification reads historical qualification artifacts and runs git rev-parse on fixed tags. Existing local build records are present.
gaps.risk: Dirty-workstation source ZIP can include machine-specific binaries/records, while clean extracted source ZIP lacks required Git tags/evidence and cannot enable qualified motif CUDA merely by rebuilding. No contaminated shipped ZIP or authority bypass is claimed.
gaps.recommended_change: Choose an explicit source/browser-only or independently qualified CUDA distribution. Exclude machine-local assets, retain production-imported test contracts, and define verified release qualification bundle/identity or documented Git/evidence prerequisites for CUDA.
gaps.security_impact: Local records are consistency evidence, not publisher authenticity. No secret disclosure or shipped contaminated ZIP is claimed.
gaps.performance_impact: Predictable portable payload and fail-closed backend availability.
acceptance_criteria: Clean and populated-workspace source packages exclude local/build assets and preserve contract imports.
Extraction proves browser-only/unavailable mode without Git/evidence; documentation is truthful.
CUDA-enabled distribution verifies exact release source/binary/environment/evidence without weakening qualification or depending accidentally on excluded Git/artifacts.

gaps.title: Release documentation and qualification provenance need additive reconciliation
gaps.current_behavior: Final JSON/browser records say PASS but qualifiedCommit=null/releaseEligible=false for historical working tree. Current authoritatively qualified tag and merge exist; README/release notes predate dynamic support. Source inventory mixes CRLF checkout and LF Git-blob hashes.
gaps.risk: Consumers may misread current qualification or fail reproducibility byte checks. This does not invalidate the user-authoritative baseline.
gaps.recommended_change: Add release manifest binding b24c4e3 and 54dd4d3, archive bytes, source byte policy and evidence ancestry; update release docs without rewriting Scope 5 history.
gaps.security_impact: Never mark blocked bf0240a qualified, move tags or silently normalize executable qualification hashes.
gaps.performance_impact: Makes clean extraction and deployment claims verifiable.
acceptance_criteria: Manifest distinguishes historical blocked checkpoint, final qualified tag and integration merge.
LF/CRLF source-byte policy documented; exact deployed native hashes qualify separately.
Public docs state real limits and supported environment.

gaps.title: Reproducible scripts exist without tracked CI orchestration
gaps.current_behavior: Full Node runner, lint/build/package checks and live qualification harnesses exist; no tracked .github workflow. GPU/browser evidence is workstation-specific.
gaps.risk: Repeatability relies on manual execution; public runners cannot substantiate RTX5060 sm120 qualification.
gaps.recommended_change: Add CPU CI for regressions/build/package contracts; protected matching GPU runner or manual signed release evidence for real native/browser/model paths.
gaps.security_impact: Never execute untrusted PR native code on a credentialed GPU release host; artifact identity and source revision required.
gaps.performance_impact: Continuous regression signals and stable benchmark provenance.
acceptance_criteria: CPU CI reproducibly runs lockfile tests/lint/both builds/package integrity.
GPU gates explicitly skip as unavailable on public CPU runners.
Release cannot pass on fixtures labelled as real CUDA.

gaps.title: Abrupt crash and deployment recovery remain incompletely qualified
gaps.current_behavior: Graceful cancellation/close/group cleanup and integrity rechecks exist. Crash orphan/temp cleanup, active-kernel driver reset/OOM and Windows effective ACLs are not established by current live cases.
gaps.risk: Multi-hour operation can leave temp/process state or fail recovery unpredictably; current cancellation evidence was immediate, not confirmed active kernel interruption.
gaps.recommended_change: Specify crash/restart cleanup and observable failure classes; run controlled recovery qualification on dedicated hardware and Windows/WSL deployment.
gaps.security_impact: New session invalidates old handles/approval/results; cleanup must only affect owned files/processes.
gaps.performance_impact: Operational reliability under failure; no unlimited automatic retry.
acceptance_criteria: Crash/restart requires fresh discovery and exact reauthorization.
Controlled native failure/OOM/reset yields no accepted result or Apply mutation.
Owned orphan cleanup and Windows ACL policy are verified/documented.

gaps.title: Batching has plausible value but unqualified composition semantics
gaps.current_behavior: Only one pending GraphMutationPlan/revision is authoritative; no general multi-revision composition interface. Existing multi-operation plan is already analyzed as one transition.
gaps.risk: Combining revisions or already applied updates can confuse base/proposed lineage, approvals and delta authority.
gaps.recommended_change: Defer automatic batching. If measured user need exists, explicitly compose draft plans against one unchanged exact base into a fresh revision, derive final-state diff and request new confirmations.
gaps.security_impact: No multi-current pending state, replay, reused approval or summed cross-base delta; DELETE_THEN_INSERT and collision policy unchanged.
gaps.performance_impact: Can amortize process/transfer only if update bursts dominate and final affected work stays favorable.
acceptance_criteria: Proceed only after measured burst amortization justifies complexity.
Composition matches sequential pure preview final state against same base.
Superseded approvals/results reject; one separate Apply commits exactly once.
